title: [dogfood:P1] Federation forwards deliveries WITHOUT auth credentials — link to an auth-enabled relay 401s
detail: Verified: relay A (CR_AUTH_TOKEN set, CR_FED_LINKS=http://127.0.0.1:8898) POST /agents/agent-b/inbox for a remote agent -> 401 {"error":"missing Authorization header"} in 0.9ms — A forwarded to B without any Bearer header and relayed B's 401 back verbatim. There is NO fed-link auth mechanism in the env surface (no CR_FED_TOKEN/secret variable exists); WEBHOOK-DELIVERY.md §8 promised 'outbound authenticated link (shared secret header v1)'. Federation is unusable against any token-protected remote relay — the README-documented default posture. Fix direction: Add shared-secret header auth for fed links (CR_FED_TOKEN env sent as X-Crier-Fed-Auth or Bearer on forwarded requests), per spec §8 open-decision #4 which already recommended it.

title: [dogfood:P1] Fed link down = instant silent 404 drop — no CR_FED_MAX_HOLD_S hold, no durable queue, no ERROR frame
detail: Verified: killed relay B, delivered to remote agent-b via A -> {"error":"agent not found"} HTTP 404 in 0.0005s (B's cached agent table still listed agent-b, so A tried to forward, connection refused, gave up immediately). CR_FED_MAX_HOLD_S=60 was set on A and the call did NOT hold. B restarted + re-registered afterwards: the message was nowhere (A and B inboxes empty). WEBHOOK-DELIVERY.md §8 promises 'Link down -> durable queue at source; ERROR after CR_FED_MAX_HOLD_S (default 300s)' — none of the three behaviors exist in this path. Fix direction: Implement fed-link outbound queue + hold timer (retry forward until CR_FED_MAX_HOLD_S, then ERROR to sender / sender inbox), or remove the promise from the spec.

title: [dogfood:P1] Async webhook delivery silently drops after retries exhausted — no ERROR frame, no dead-letter
detail: Verified: agent with async webhook to an always-500 endpoint; watched X-Crier-Retry go 2,3,4,5 at 30s intervals (CR_WEBHOOK_REDELIVER_S=5 did not change the cadence either), then server log 'webhook: delivery dropped (retries exhausted)' — sender's inbox stayed EMPTY (checked repeatedly), no ERROR WEBHOOK_FAILED frame/message ever arrived, no status endpoint exposes the drop. WEBHOOK-DELIVERY.md §3/§4: 'retries -> ERROR WEBHOOK_FAILED{status, retries}'. A fire-and-forget sender can lose messages with zero signal. Fix direction: On exhaustion, deliver an ERROR-kind message to the sender's inbox (or a dead-letter table + stats field), carrying message_id + last status.

title: [mesh:P1] mesh peers absent from the HTTP registry are silently dropped from the route table — REQUESTs hang forever, no ERROR frame
detail: A WebSocket mesh peer that completes /mesh/connect + REGISTER but never did POST /agents is not routable: REQUESTs to it hang until client timeout with no ERROR frame (live-verified twice, incl. with both-registered control passing at 43ms). title: [obs:P1] message path is undebuggable: no request correlation id, zero logging on relay accept + webhook dispatch
detail: Deep-debug audit 2026-09-14: the two hottest events on a message bus — a relay publish accepted and a webhook delivery dispatched — emit ZERO log lines (internal/relay/handler.go: 0 slog calls; internal/webhook/driver.go: 0). There is no request correlation id (X-Request-Id or otherwise), so a 202 in the access log cannot be tied to the later webhook POST, guard decision, or FEDERATION_FAILED notice. Federation is the counter-example: hold.go logs the entire lifecycle (held, retry-persist, recovered, failed) and it is a joy to debug. Fix: (1) middleware generates/propagates X-Request-Id, echoes it on responses, and every slog line in the request path carries it; (2) deliver-202, webhook dispatch + outcome, and guard decision log one line each carrying message_id + agent_id + sender; (3) mesh REGISTER/REQUEST-drop and WS subscribe/unsubscribe lifecycle log at debug level.

detail: During tick 268 the E2E battery was launched on the standard port 18767 and reported "BATTERY: 14/14 probes passed" rc=0 against a process that was NOT the binary under test. Step 5 (the PATCH, HTTP 200) returns last_seen=2026-09-14T23:19:17.600589-05:00 while step 6 (GET immediately after) returns 2026-09-14T23:19:20.31042-05:00, i.e. the response body is rendered from the caller's in-memory copy rather than from the row that was just written. The in-memory backend is further behind: it never advances last_seen at all on update (Update writes capabilities/webhook/guard only), so a client cannot use last_seen from a PATCH response to confirm the write. No data is lost and delivery is unaffected — this is a wire-contract inconsistency, not the DF-CRIER-151 failure shape. Fix direction: have both stores refresh agent.LastSeen (and the other persisted defaults) on the caller's object before the handler renders the response, with a test asserting the PATCH response's last_seen equals the subsequent GET's.

title: [dogfood:P2] Deliver 202 body is documented as the federation-hold shape only, so the guard field on webhook async/batch accepts is undocumented
detail: internal/registry/handler.go:615-618 answers async/batch webhook deliveries with 202 deliverResponse{id, guard}, but docs/openapi.yaml (and the generated cmd/server copy) declare the 202 body as the federation-hold shape only (required: [status, id, target, max_hold_s]). DF-CRIER-158 made an allow verdict that carries a risk marker visible on the deliver response, which makes this gap load-bearing: the guard object (and plain id) a webhook sender receives on a 202 has no documented contract, and a tester writing a client from the spec cannot know which arm of the 202 to expect. Fix: model the 202 body as oneOf [federation hold, webhook accept] and document id/guard on the webhook-accept arm. Filed by foreman tick 269 from the DF-CRIER-158 worker's out-of-scope report; premise verified by the foreman in handler.go:615-618 + docs/openapi.yaml:560-580 before filing.

title: [CI:P2] TestDeliver_Blocking_TimeoutIs504/endpoint_hangs_past_the_budget flaked red on tick-271 board push (run 35038607923) — 200+empty reply instead of 504; passes 58/58 clean-cache reruns locally; client timeout is driver-global not per-attempt
detail: CI run 35038607923 (push of board commit 3c0242c) failed Build & Test on internal/registry: TestDeliver_Blocking_TimeoutIs504/endpoint_hangs_past_the_budget got status=200 body={"id":"...","transport":"webhook","reply":""} instead of the expected 504. The endpoint sleeps 2s, budget is 100ms, so the first attempt should time out and DeliverBlocking should return the 'timed out' error -> 504. A 200 with an empty reply means c.http.Do returned a completed (empty-body) 2xx within the budget, i.e. the client's http.Client.Timeout cut the hanging attempt even though cfg.TimeoutMs=100 was far below the next retry's needs. Foreman repro: passes -count=8 (residue), then 20/20 isolated subtest and 30/30 full-package after go clean -testcache (58/58 total) on this host. Code read: webhook.Client has a DRIVER-GLOBAL timeout (NewClient(timeout, secret)); the blocking attempt request carries NO per-attempt context deadline (postBody builds without ctx), so per-attempt waits rely on the global client timeout only; handler.go:590 maps req.TimeoutMs->budget=100ms correctly. Also verify whether deliverHarness's TimeoutMs:100 override reaches the client (webhook.Config.TimeoutMs) or only sets the budget. Fix candidates: (a) give the blocking attempt context.WithTimeout(remaining budget) so an attempt can never overrun the budget; (b) harden the test (longer hang, wall-clock assert); (c) check no package-level shared webhook.Client with a short timeout bleeds across tests in the same package. Evidence trail: tick 271 audit event 451; gh run 35038607923 failed-step log; internal/webhook/driver.go DeliverBlocking; internal/webhook/webhook.go postBody; internal/registry/handler.go:590.

reasoning.note: foreman tick 271 — post-push CI red on a push carrying ZERO code touching this path; local clean-cache 58/58 green; real race candidate filed per CI-health mandate

worker_summary: DeliverBlocking now bounds each ATTEMPT by the remaining budget: remaining := time.Until(deadline) (clamped to 1ns when <=0) is passed to a new Client.PostContext via context.WithTimeout, and postBody builds the request with http.NewRequestWithContext. Before this change the attempt was bounded only by the driver-global http.Client.Timeout fixed at NewClient(timeout, secret) - Config.TimeoutMs never reached the client - so a delivery with timeout_ms=100 could run for the full global timeout and, when the endpoint's late 2xx won the race, be reported to the caller as a SUCCESS. Post/PostBatch keep their signatures and delegate with context.Background() (no caller churn). Deterministic regression test TestDeliverBlocking_AttemptBoundedByRemainingBudget (2s endpoint, 10s global client timeout, 100ms budget) FAILS on the pre-fix driver with 'err = nil, reply = late-reply after 2.002s - an over-budget endpoint 2xx was reported as a SUCCESS' and PASSES after. Previously red shape green 3x consecutively (13/13 packages), TestDeliver_Blocking_TimeoutIs504 -count=10 ok; judge PASS 2c095725.
review_notes: Root cause was NOT the filed hypothesis (a client timeout cutting a hanging attempt): the attempt was unbounded by the caller's budget and the test's 2s endpoint sleep photo-finished the harness's driver-global 2s http.Client.Timeout, so a loaded run accepted a 200-empty-reply as success. Fix is in the production path (no test was weakened). Semantics preserved: ctx deadline stays Retryable -> 504, non-retryable rejections and unmappable 2xx stay ErrPermanent -> 502.

title: [guard:P0] circuit breaker never re-arms after a failed probe — every request becomes an unthrottled probe
detail: internal/guard/circuit.go:72-77 — recordFailure only stamps openedAt[key] when absent; after the first cooldown elapses and the probe fails, openedAt stays at the original trip time so open() returns false forever. Result: one probe per cooldown becomes unthrottled probing of a dead provider. External report includes a failing test (TestCircuit_FailedProbeReopens) that reproduces at 40e9b1f. Fix per reporter: when streak >= threshold and openedAt is absent or older than cooldown, restamp openedAt[key]=now.

title: [obs:P0] panicked requests never reach the access log — Logging lacks defer, Recovery sits outside it
detail: internal/middleware/middleware.go:18-25 + cmd/server/main.go:96-99 — chain is RequestID->Auth->Recovery->Logging; a handler panic unwinds through Logging before its slog.Info runs, so the 500 is served but never access-logged (only the bare 'panic recovered' line, no method/path/request_id — undermines DF-CRIER-141 correlation). External report includes failing test TestLogging_PanickedRequestIsLogged reproduced at 40e9b1f. Fix: defer the access-log write in Logging (status 500 on recovery) or move Recovery inside Logging; pass request_id into the panic line.

title: [followup:P2] RemoteStore.List launders every decode/transport failure into an empty registry — a silent zero-agent answer for the MCP bridge
detail: internal/registry/remote.go:245-255 List swallows EVERY decode error: `if err := s.do(http.MethodGet, "/agents", nil, &out); err != nil { return []*Agent{} }`. A decode failure, a 401/403 and a 5xx are therefore all indistinguishable from an EMPTY REGISTRY on the bridge surface, and the failure is silent (no log, no error returned to the caller). Reproduce at c4f2f04: point a RemoteStore at a server that answers /agents with a shape it cannot decode (or with a 500) and observe List() returning an empty slice with no error and no log line. Acceptance: RemoteStore.List stops laundering failures into an empty slice - either the decode error is surfaced to the caller (an error return, or a distinguishable sentinel) or it is at minimum logged once per occurrence with the status/body context, while a genuinely empty registry still returns an empty slice; an erroring server must be distinguishable from an empty one by a bridge caller, and focused tests cover both the empty-registry case and the undecodable-response case.
